catalog_quote: 2.4 声調 パナ語は各音節に固有の声調を持つ。その状況は他の苗瑶語と同様で、祖語の4つの声調（A～Dで表示）から分岐してできた8つの声調調類（音韻的に対立のある超分節音的な特徴、パナ語では主としてピッチのパタンで実現する：1～8で表示）を持つ。その調類と調値（5段階表記：5が最も高く、1が最も低い）は以下のとおり。 [table] 祖語の声調 A | B | C | D / 調類 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 / 調値 24 12 44 21 35 22 45 42. [Taguchi 2012, p.217: 2.5 声調 (Tone) パナ語は各音節に表4に示した8つの声調のいずれかを持つ。その調類と調値（5段階表記：5が最も高く、1が最も低い）は以下のとおり。 表4 パナ語の声調: 調類 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 / 調値 24 12 44 31 35 33(2) 45 42.] [tr.: 'Pana has an inherent tone on every syllable. The situation is the same as in the other Miao-Yao languages: it has eight tone categories (phonologically contrastive suprasegmental features, realized in Pana mainly as pitch patterns; labelled 1-8) that split from the four tones of the proto-language (labelled A-D). Their categories and values (five-level notation: 5 highest, 1 lowest) are as follows.' / 2012: 'Every syllable of Pana carries one of the eight tones shown in Table 4.']

The reported translation is accurate. Surrounding section (pp.159-161, read from the scanned file plus the page scan): §2 音韻構造 covers 2.1 consonants (three series of stops/affricates, lateral plosive, two…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Syllable-tone language: each syllable bears one of eight lexical tones (13, 313, 44, 31, 35, 22, 55, 53 per Chen 2001 via zh.wikipedia; Taguchi gives his own 5-level values). Neither Taguchi 2001 nor his fuller 2012 phonology section says anything about word stress or accent. Second-hand (zh.wikipedia < Chen 2001: 71-72): no tone sandhi and 'no obvious 轻声' (no clearly reduced/neutral-tone syllables), although Chen 2013's transcriptions (via Hsiu 2015's spreadsheet) write the nominal prefixes la-, ka- and the suffix -tsai with 0-initial (weak-syllable) tone values.
new_statements.exceptions: None in Taguchi. Possible weak/atonal prefix syllables (la⁰⁴-, ka⁰³-) appear in Chen 2013's notation but no accessible source states a rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone is assigned per syllable; Taguchi's texts are segmented by intonation and pause only, with no word- or phrase-stress marking.
new_statements.identity_note: Taguchi's data (2001-2015) are from one consultant, 呉昌凡, of 下排村 Xiapai village, 长安营乡 (former 岩寨乡), 城步苗族自治县 Chengbu, Hunan; language self-named pa53 na313 (Taguchi: /pa8 na4/). Same language as Glottolog pana1310 'Pa Na' (Chinese 巴那语, also written 坝那语 in Li Yunbing 2017 and Duan & Liu 2015). No ISO code.

Fuchu, Tokyo: Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa (ILCAA), Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. ISBN 978-4-86337-267-2 (printed '987-4-86337-267-2'). CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
sources.tag: read: notes on tone
sources.note: Describes another variety (Glottolog hmon1336). All Hmong-Mien lects are tone languages; four proto-tones *A-*D; Tone-split 1 (by devoicing of initials) gives A1/A2.. D1/D2, Tone-split 2 (by de-aspiration) further splits the 1-series; lects classed as Type 1 (no split: Luobohe Miao), Type 2a-e (only split 1; 2-e = all categories split, ~64% of lects), Type 3 (both splits, southern area). No per-language tone values; Pa Na not discussed by name.

tone.quote: All the lects belonging to Hmong-Mien language family are tone languages. Proto-Hmong-Mien has been reconstructed with four proto-tone categories (Purnell 1970, Ratliff 2010). They are designated by one of the tone marks: *A, *B, *C, and *D (see Table 1). In most Hmong-Mien lects, each proto-tone splits into two through devoicing of initials (Tone-split 1).
tone.summary: Family-level statement only (Hmong-Mien lects tonal; 4 proto-tones split by onset devoicing into up to 8+ categories); nothing Pa Na-specific.
tone.says: All Hmong-Mien lects are tone languages; four proto-tones *A-*D; Tone-split 1 (by devoicing of initials) gives A1/A2.. No per-language tone values; Pa Na not discussed by name.
